comment: Skromne cares about his students' wellbeing. He's very flexible with late work, but posts assignments  late or changes due dates and doesn't tell the class. Lectures are boring and the tests questions would be unrelated. We had test corrections because exam averages were very low. He's very homework heavy and his lab lectures go on forever.

Kind person, but the class is overwhelming. BIOL 200 has so many lab assignments + capstone, you also submit summary notes every week for the assigned chapter. Lectures are hard to follow & the order we learn things in is questionable. Exams sometimes don't cover what we reviewed, and they are hard ash. Overall difficult class, but not impossible.

Let's start with the good. Dr.Skromne gives tests corrections and that comes in handy because his exams are difficult. He also allows corrections on his practice exams. He's extremely flexible with accepting late work. His labs are long and he sometimes goes overtime. Lectures are long and boring. I would still take this class again.

The course is primarily reading and discussion based. A big part of your grade comes from how well you can discuss/explain the reading, so it involves a lot of prep work between classes if you want to get the full participation points. If you keep on top of all of the readings, the exams are very manageable.

Skromne is a very sweet man & tries to make the class low on stress. However, he is not a good teacher. His lecturers are always confusing & unclear along with his tests. His grading scale for assignments are never clear leaving many students confused. He gives corrections on exams only b/c of the low exam scores everyone gets due his teaching.

He's actually a caring professor who wants his students to do well. The class itself is very work intensive, and lecture can be confusing at times. The primary issue isn't Dr. Skromne, but all of the biology professors that formatted the course. All of the Bio 200 professor have the exact same teaching style/method.

The course itself is designed badly, so I understand he wasn't given much to work with. However, there were issues with organization (rubric for a 2 month long project not posted until 2 hours before presentation), tests do not always accurately reflect class content, and students don't feel comfortable/respected asking for help.

While I can appreciate his attempts to make students think analytically, Dr. Skromne taught this class with a stunning lack of organization (two major projects from completely different course modules ended up being due during the final week). There were also times when he was rather condescending, and his attempted "jokes" were sometimes hurtful.

Neurodevelopment is a complex topic, which is then exacerbated by Skromne's complex way of setting up the class. Students read scientific papers on the topic before even reading the textbook chapter on it. So, students have no idea what the paper is about and are expected to annotate it as if they do. Criteria to be successful in work is unclear.

Dr. Skromne is an amazing professor. He is so passionate about teaching and getting his students passionate about what they are learning. Tests can be challenging, but they aren't worth very much of your overall grade. Labs are fun and very interesting. Great person and great teacher.

I appreciate him SO much. He's a great professor who does amazing research and knows what he is talking about. He is also super nice and candid. He wants you to do well but pushes you to achieve that. To do well, pay attention to textbook readings and ask him if you dont understand. His lectures may or may not be your style. Prepare well for exams!

As a person, I think Dr. Skromne is really nice and does genuinely care about his students. However, as a professor, most of the lectures were pretty boring, and the way he taught just did not engage most students. Any practice tests that he gave did not represent the real tests at all. If you want to do well in this class, ask a lot of questions.

Neurodevelopment is an awesome subject and the class itself has potential if it was taught by someone else. Skromne is very bad at explaining things and the papers assigned were, for the most part, unreasonable to read and summarize. Most of the class had no idea what was going on. Not the nicest prof to deal with. Avoid if you can!
